approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from a session-local archive and uses two predictors to select which offspring receive scores. A count-fingerprint Gaussian process supplies a predictive mean, correlated sampled residuals and the original mean-based eligibility rule. A fixed tree model learns raw score differences between accepted molecules and averages predictions over every accepted reference. Before each announced batch, the Parent mixes these two locations with a convex weight fitted only to errors of predictions made before earlier paid labels. Real accepted scores update the archive, survivors and breeding population.
approach.novelty: This control removes the learned pair correction from every active allocation, making the original GP mean the sole active location while both expert fits and the original chronological weight calculation continue passively. It asks whether the correction contributes to adaptive endpoints on its actual weighted host. There are no evaluated same-Parent siblings in the brief. Earlier reference-support, reciprocity, scalar-potential and residual-dependence experiments changed other operations or other hosts; none supplies this GP-only adaptive comparison.

hypothesis: Implement one causal null of the active learned pair-correction consumer inside m-000000000005 on n-b8387b35c526. On every successful allocation, with original raw-unit GP mean g_t(x), unchanged all-reference raw-pair location a_t(x), and the Parent exact learned weight w_t, replace the active location g_t(x)+w_t*(a_t(x)-g_t(x)) by g_t(x). The active sample is the already computed original g_t(x)+r_t(x), with r_t=score_scale*(original_normals @ actual_successful_original_factor.T). Retain this residual amplitude and correlation, its normal tensor call/shape/order, original GP mean K3/M40 eligibility, per-position availability and stable generation-index ties. Both predictors still fit exactly the Parent targets/settings on the complete current-session accepted archive. The passive ledger remains A=sum((y_j-g_j)*(a_j-g_j)), B=sum((a_j-g_j)^2), in the Parent serial float64 update order over previous optimizer purchases only, with w=clip(A/B,0,1), w=0 for no prior paid prediction or exact-zero B. Freeze the weight and all expert/mixture predictions before each announcement; commit once only after its complete real accepted feedback. Do not replace the learned weight by zero or refit on current labels. Initial records train the experts but never the weight. Keep g+w*(a-g)+r and its sequential choices as a fully recorded passive policy on the Child state. Only active pair influence is removed; the pair learner and learned coefficient form the inseparable conditional contribution target. Their individual values, the whole GP selector, residuals and eligibility are not separately priced.

finding_summary.headline: Removing the pair correction gains 0.04186, refuting its retained endpoint benefit on this host.
finding_summary.insights:
This resolves the missing adaptive control: the correction can improve average prediction error without improving purchases or final best scores on its weighted host. The earlier result that weighting improved the pair-only predictor remains intact. Here, the unchanged chronological and convex squared-loss operations continued passively, with no newly adopted literature operation; their source guarantees do not transfer to dependent adaptive batches. The experiment prices the pair model and its learned coefficient together as an active correction, not either component alone. A ranking model or acquisition rule aligned with the extreme-score objective is the kind of method that could address the observed calibration-to-selection mismatch, but this run does not establish which replacement would help.

The method also retains a search limitation beyond that consumer. Only 238 of 2,175 late purchases beat their generating parents, versus 261 for the weighted Parent, and late incumbent advances fell from 82 to 76 despite the endpoint gain. The molecular audit shows local concentration rather than universal scaffold collapse: 1,668 typed scaffolds coexist with only five and seven generic scaffolds in two high-score task subsets. Large purchases of at least 50 heavy atoms fell from 245 to 46, while fragments of six or fewer atoms rose from 62 to 98. Fragment-excluded similarity also fell, so smaller molecules and fewer scaffolds do not imply one uniformly narrower search. Coherent core/linker proposal operators could address this uneven access to alternative structures; the data do not establish chemical mediation or promise a gain. Unusual heteroatom bonds and unassigned stereochemistry remain. The finite-panel result narrows the value of this retained correction under these conditions and leaves broader predictor, consumer and proposal designs open.
finding_summary.results:
The removal executed exactly in all 435 batches: active means, sampled fields and ordered choices matched the original GP law, while both predictors and the original chronological weight updates continued. Passive weights were zero in 55 batches, interior in 376 and one in four. The intervention changed 349 selected sets and bought 1,111 molecules outside the passive mixture selections, so this was an exposed adaptive control. All 4,350 prediction–label joins and 4,200 subsequent-fit joins were complete; the final 150 purchases were correctly censored for later fitting.

Mean final score rose from 0.565170 to 0.607030, an issued paired gain of 0.041861. All three seed macros improved, by 0.092358, 0.010303 and 0.022921; ten task/seed endpoints improved and five declined. Seed dispersion increased from 0.007309 to 0.030175. With isolation and exposure established, the gain exceeds the registered +0.002 boundary and supports negative conditional contribution of the retained pair correction. The directional benefit hypothesis is refuted; execution succeeded. The separate formal criterion requiring a different code Parent is inapplicable.

On the actual GP purchases, the passive mixture still had lower mean squared error than GP, 0.010982 versus 0.011599, but lower within-batch ordering accuracy, 70.08% versus 70.65%. Neither diagnostic supplies rewards for molecules the passive policy would have bought.

molecular.headline: Compact ring-rich families, frequent unusual heteroatom bonds, more tiny fragments and no specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen original Child and fifteen published code-Parent trajectories were read for frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and all five issued tasks. Each node supplies 4,350 optimizer purchases and 150 supplied initial observations; every row remains in its cell audit. Initial rows are identical in every paired cell and are excluded from aggregate purchase descriptors and similarity. The request separately establishes complete Child evaluation and complete code-Parent pairing with n-b8387b35c526, with no profile-mismatched seeds. No path or objective is missing. These are accepted scored purchases; the trajectories do not enumerate the full unevaluated proposal pools. All signed endpoint cells are retained in per_task. This report makes no mechanism, contribution, reliability, efficacy or node-selection judgment. The chemistry includes fused aromatic carboxamides, linked N-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles, aryl/saturated-amine assemblies, bridged carbonyl N-rings and fluorinated carbonyl/imino heterocycles. Digest ring-closure presence rates are 0.9713–0.9862 and aromatic-token presence rates 0.9644–0.9770; these count molecule-level SMILES features, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. RDKit finds aromatic atoms in 4,226 purchases and an empty acyclic Murcko scaffold in 95. Median heavy atoms are 28 with range 1–96 versus Parent 30 and 1–118. Both source-defined size tails are retained: counts at <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms are Child 91/98/46/44 versus Parent 60/62/245/229. Smaller bulk size therefore coexists with more tiny fragments. Typed/generic Murcko counts including empty are 1,668/952 versus Parent 1,874/1,095; local high-score families are often narrower than these pooled counts suggest. Within-cell count-Tanimoto means are Child 0.5979745477772664 versus Parent 0.6242320463952082; excluding <=6-heavy-atom molecules gives 0.6249222626738333 versus 0.641811143438338. Within-batch means are 0.6852254822759881 versus 0.7062740506878608, or 0.7157196006976139 versus 0.7260179739677268 after exclusion. These are radius-2 chirality-aware 2,048-count Morgan dot-product generalized Tanimotos, pair-count weighted only within each session or actual ten-purchase batch; no cross-session pairs or independent-trial claims are made. Lower similarity and fewer scaffolds can coexist and neither measures chemical utility. N-halogen bonds appear in 888 purchases on each side; O-halogen Child/Parent counts are 162/422, S-halogen 107/62 and O-O single bonds 118/63. Nitroso graph flags appear in 242 Child purchases versus none in the Parent, concentrated in one task/seed family. Carbon-centered atoms with at least two double bonds occur in 5 purchases versus 84; the subset with central carbon and both double bonds in rings is 3 versus 53. Sulfur-centered counts are separately 77 versus 176, not treated as allene liabilities. The <=4-cycle/all-atoms-aromatic-perceived flag occurs in 170 purchases versus 175 and does not establish that the small cycle or all its bonds are aromatic. No Child or Parent purchase has nonzero formal charge, assigned tetrahedral configuration or specified double-bond geometry. Child has 4,388 unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,578 molecules, versus Parent 5,714 in 2,646. These are representational gaps, not established activity requirements; neutral depiction does not specify solution protonation. Chemistry chips describe recognizable organic motifs mixed with unusual local bonds and unresolved configurations; no synthesis, stability, ADME, binding or safety measurements are supplied. Top/bottom-29 per cell and top/bottom-87 per task are explicitly score-ordered descriptive subsets, with seed/evaluation tie breaking; final-ten records are kept separately. Pooling may concentrate a subset in one seed. per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by compact indole-like fused aromatic carboxamides, often linked to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Seed 0's best carries a vinyl thioether and methoxy group; seed 1's best combines an aryl bromide, an N-fluorinated indole-like nitrogen and a pyridyl carboxamide; seed 2's best is a trimethyl indole-like alpha-ketoamide with N-chlorination. The three best molecules each have three perceived aromatic rings. Recognizable aromatic amide frameworks coexist with chemically unusual N-halogenation. This is primarily ring substitution around a local family, not absence of ring generation. Across 870 purchases, heavy-atom median/range are 25/1–47, versus Parent 25/1–41; median perceived rings/aromatic atoms are 3/15. Typed/generic scaffolds including empty are 187/70 versus Parent 296/112. Recorded maxima in seed order 0/1/2 are Child 0.423482167177128/0.4387992465191/0.450504369815676 versus Parent 0.434963536766715/0.482817138637361/0.440333660348919; Child best evaluations are 290/97/261. All issued Child-minus-Parent endpoint cells, including adverse values, are seed 0: -0.0114813695895872; seed 1: -0.0440178921182609; seed 2: +0.0101707094667567. These retain the supplied comparison boundary; they do not judge mechanism or contribution.
liabilities: N-F/N-Cl/N-Br substitutions occur at heteroaromatic or amide nitrogens, including high-scoring molecules; their stability and preparation are not established by sanitizable graphs.
The low end includes peroxide-linked duplicate cores and tiny fragments; the same output does not uniformly preserve coherent medicinal-sized structures.
missing_features: The observed high region gives little coverage of conventional non-N-halogen versions of its high-scoring ring/amide arrangements; the strong local N-halogen association leaves those alternatives inadequately resolved, rather than proving they would improve the score.
Broader core/linker replacements at the retained compact scale are weakly represented in the high subset. No named missing target pharmacophore can be established from these labels alone.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
